texts: good. the emergence lands in full - the wraith witness, day 120 and Year 1, the cove's water as the source it came out of, the dim burning on the night of day 111, the stated because-link and the anteriority ordering between the two. One caveat you cannot write around: 'day 120 of Year 1' goes into the calendar day-of-month slot as (Day 120), because the translator has no day-of-year term.

good. the burning and the emergence both reuse the symbols from the previous sentence, so 'the emergence' resolves rather than minting a second event, and the sentence adds exactly one new thing - the measured nine-day gap.

good. the seeing, Marra as the one who sees and the wraith as what is seen, the 'first' ordinal on the seeing, her station with her as its possessor, the station's nearness to the Cove Stair, and the station as the vantage point are all carried.
good. a plain past walking event with Marra as the mover and the Stilllight Lantern as its goal.

bad: 'already' is dropped. 'was already at the Stilllight Lantern' is a bare position clause, which mints no event, and the 'already' tag needs an eventuality to attach to - so all that survives is that Bevin was at the lantern, losing the point that he was there before Marra got there. Write 'Bevin Coombe had already reached the Stilllight Lantern.' - the finite verb gives 'already' a carrier, and the past perfect additionally orders his arrival before Marra's walk.

good. 'was lit' is read as a past lighting event with the lantern as the thing lit, which is what the instruction set prescribes for a participle after 'be'; note that what gets recorded is a lighting having happened, not a standing 'is alight' state.
good. 'ground' lemmatizes to grind, the bare plural object mints a feather group that the next sentences reuse, and the grinding correctly treats the feathers as changed rather than merely handled.

good. the scattering reuses that same feather group and keeps doer, object, place and tense; 'around' survives only as the event's location at the lantern, so the encircling shape is not separately recorded - no loss here, since the next sentence states the warding outright.

good. the feathers are the doer, the lantern is what is warded, and 'against the wraith' is kept as its own link on the warding event, with both the feather group and the wraith reusing their earlier symbols.
good. plain past approach event, the wraith approaching the lantern.
good. 'turned away' is kept whole as the phrasal verb turn_away - never split, never swapped for a single-word synonym - with the lantern as the thing it turned from.

good. the whole drain event (class, the wraith as doer, the lantern as object, past tense) sits inside one strength-0 bundle, which is the right denial shape, and the lantern's own identity stays outside the denial.
